seal.statement: Reading has shown that Lagrange has no committed Raft membership: the liferaft library's join and leave edit a local in-memory peer array, quorum is computed from that local array, and each node reconciles its own array from cached service rows, so safe dynamic membership - the part of Raft that is hardest to get right - is being attempted outside Raft. The owner has decided that no Lagrange-owned committed-membership protocol is built on liferaft, and that it is first to be proved whether the TiKV raft-rs core, reached through the existing raft-logic WASM work, provides the missing primitive cleanly; the core is the asset under evaluation, not raft-logic's high-level JavaScript API. The question this quest answers is the owner's: can raft-rs through WASM make Raft membership a replicated fact which remains correct despite divergent Lagrange metadata caches, crash and restart, and concurrent configuration-change attempts, at an acceptable Multi-Raft cost. It changes nothing in production and switches nothing. First it turns the reading about liferaft into measurement on the real provider and the real peer reconciliation: for the same partition and the same underlying state, one node whose cache says the peers are A, B and C and another whose cache says A, B and D each report what their Raft instance believes its voting configuration and quorum to be, with no consensus operation having occurred; nothing replicated or generational records the configuration; and term and vote are read before a crash and after a restart through the actual production persistence path. Second it states the minimum backend contract Lagrange needs, derived mechanically from what the partition service and the provider seam call today plus the configuration operations they lack. Third, because the published raft-logic binding exposes a RawNode-shaped surface but no proposal or application of configuration changes at all, it extends a fork of that binding, kept on the test side of this repository and not upstreamed, to expose the raft-rs primitives themselves - proposing a version-two configuration change, applying a committed one, identifying committed configuration entries, and observing the resulting configuration state - and no convenience membership methods, so that the policy of adding a learner, waiting for it to catch up, promoting it and removing the old voter stays in Lagrange. It drives the core directly and deterministically, with manual ticks and in-process message passing: a stable three-voter group; a sequential replacement in Lagrange's style, voters A B C gaining learner D, D catching up, D promoted, B removed; separately a joint replacement by one version-two change from A B C to A C D, entering the joint configuration, committing it and leaving it; and for each what it costs and what semantics it provides, without deciding which Lagrange should use. It does not require byte-identical configuration on every peer at every instant: it requires that after the relevant configuration entry has been committed and applied on each surviving peer their configuration state converges to the same configuration without consulting Lagrange service rows, and that in the intermediate period quorum and membership decisions come from the core's own configuration state. It restarts a peer at each of nine boundaries - proposed but not persisted, persisted but not committed, committed but not applied by the application, configuration change applied but the returned configuration state not durably recorded, configuration state recorded but Ready not advanced, Ready advanced, joint configuration entered, joint configuration committed, joint configuration left - under the invariant that restart must reconstruct the same Raft membership from durable Raft state alone and no service-row cache may repair it, with the Ready and persistence ordering of the raft-rs model, in which the configuration state returned by applying a change becomes the durable configuration used on restore, treated as the highest-risk part of the wrapper. It shows that disagreeing service caches leave Raft membership identical. It observes, and does not prescribe, what happens when a second version-two configuration change is proposed before the first is applied: the return value, the emitted log entry, the committed entry type, the resulting configuration state, and whether the second requested change ever takes effect. It holds peer identity to a hard invariant - a stable mapping from Lagrange replica identity to a Raft peer id that survives restart and address change, distinguishes distinct replicas on one physical node, is never reassigned after deletion, reconstructs deterministically, and crosses the JavaScript boundary without the loss an ordinary number inflicts on a sixty-four-bit value. It measures Multi-Raft cost for one, one hundred and one thousand groups in the intended hosting shape, separating one-time WASM module and runtime memory from incremental bytes per RawNode and the costs of an idle tick, a step, a has-ready scan, Ready processing and a configuration change. It pins the toolchain of the checked-in fork and keeps two things apart: that the artifact tested is the artifact recorded, and whether that artifact can be reproduced. In every scenario membership is whatever the core itself reports, never something the test declares, and a scenario not driven is recorded as undriven and unanswered. It accounts for what the earlier raft-logic spike in the tree already found. Its output is one generated evaluation document with three independent conclusions derived from the results - whether the consensus core can provide correct replicated membership semantics, whether the WASM boundary can expose them safely and cheaply, and whether the existing provider and partition architecture can adopt them without pathological cost - so that a failure says whether the problem is raft-rs, WASM, the current binding or the hosting model, together with a forecast of what production could delete, labelled as a forecast. Integrating a backend into the partition service and running the formation case against it are the next stage and are not part of this quest.

text: Part A measured at seal on production owners (real liferaft, LiferaftProvider.joinPeer, reconcileRaftPeersFromCacheForService, PartitionRaftStorage, SQLiteLogAdapter over a real file, the lifecycle wiring), re-run by the lead, 3 of 3 green. (1) Same partition, same moment, no consensus operation: node A's cache {a,b,c} and node B's cache {a,b,d with d SYNCING} give two different voting configurations, each majority()=2 over its own local array; c votes on A and is unknown to B, d votes on B and is unknown to A; zero protocol writes occurred; B can reach its own majority as {b,d}; a SYNCING row is a voter. (2) The configuration is local, unreplicated and carries no generation: a join emits no write, the peer never learns it, and an append packet built before and after growing the configuration from 2 to 3 members is deeply equal - nothing in the protocol identifies or fences the configuration. (3) Term and vote on the production persistence path: a vote granted at term 7 leaves currentTerm 7 in memory only and votedFor never recorded; persistTerm, persistVotedFor, setTerm and setVotedFor have no caller in src; the durable _raft_state table holds zero rows after the granted vote; after restart currentTerm is 0 and votedFor null, so the replica may vote again in a term it already voted in. The only durable currentTerm writer is snapshot install. This is an independent Raft safety defect beyond membership. Also measured on the published raft-logic 0.3.14 binding: every u64 crosses the JS boundary as a decimal string and a JS number is rejected; one WASM runtime holds many RawNodes behind a u32 handle table; storage is MemStorage inside the module with no read-back export; bootstrap.conf_state is decoded and discarded, creation seeds voters only; no configuration surface exists; status is {lead, raftState}; the light-ready commit index cannot be written back. The earlier spike under src/raft/spike never changed membership (zero configuration-change vocabulary) and drives the JS shell with workers and wall-clock ticks; its id mapper allocates by list position, not identity. Correction to the owner-decision record: raft-logic is a devDependency.

Lead review of the first phase-2 result, then owner direction 2026-09-20 (recorded in the epic's owner-decision-raft-backend-evaluation-2026-09-20.md, second addendum): the all-green result is INVALID until repaired and independently verified. Defect found by the lead in the artifact: the six in-cycle restart boundaries were one position under six names - at conf-state-recorded-not-advanced and at ready-advanced the victim's durable record still held voters 1,2,3, learner 4, applied 1, commit 1, identical to proposed-not-persisted, because the harness fired an armed stop on the first Ready cycle rather than the cycle carrying the configuration entry, and convergence afterwards proved only follower catch-up. Owner direction, strengthening the sealed receipts restart-at-each-of-nine-boundaries, ready-persistence-ordering, minimum-backend-contract and three-verdicts and weakening none: boundaries defined relative to the configuration entry index discovered from the core's Ready, each recording its distinguishing durable and in-memory facts and proved pairwise distinct; victims restarted isolated, local restore correctness asserted before and separately from eventual convergence; follower and leader victims, measured not prescribed, under the property that restored state is exactly explainable by what was durably persisted and never invents a configuration change; nine persistence-order host mutants that must be refused, fail restart equivalence or yield a recorded unsafe result; a host contract derived from raft-rs 0.7 separating what raft-rs guarantees from what the host must guarantee; joint restart proving the complete ConfState and joint quorum semantics; the re-application result narrowed to the one idempotent case measured; sequential and joint replacement reported separately with no choice; the contract census in four categories MUST SERVE, MEMBERSHIP-LOCAL DELETE CANDIDATE, DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATION, PRODUCTION GAP with the deletion forecast counting only the second; Multi-Raft figures labelled preliminary; byte-different WASM investigated but not a consensus blocker; verdict inputs fixed, migration staying undetermined, part A kept out of its inputs. After independent approval the next quest is a minimal experimental raft-rs partition backend integration behind the provider seam, fresh clusters only; no log migration, no liferaft removal, and the membership-model-reduction implementation does not resume until that experiment reports.

Phase 2 by the Opus implementer under the lead's brief, two lead rejections and the owner's two addenda. Fork of the raft-rs 0.7 WASM binding kept test-side (raft-core: source, Cargo.lock, pinned toolchain, BUILD.md with crate checksums, built artifact, digest): raw primitives only - propose_conf_change_v2, apply_conf_change returning the core's ConfState, decode_conf_change_entry, conf_state, set_conf_state, persist_commit_index, export_persisted_state, extended status with pendingConfIndex and progress, create_node honouring bootstrap conf_state, learners and applied; no convenience membership export, asserted absent. Deterministic drives on the core: three voters; sequential replacement with a peer dying at each phase (promoting a dead learner still commits - policy stays in Lagrange); joint replacement with explicit and automatic leave (auto-leave needs a tick before has_ready), both majorities measured as required while joint; convergence after apply; part A's two disagreeing caches leave ConfState identical and are structurally unread; a second pending ConfChangeV2 is accepted and neutralised into an empty normal entry (types 2,0) and never takes effect; re-delivering an enter-joint entry to a peer already joint is refused by the core. Restart matrix after the lead found the first version vacuous: nine boundaries times follower and leader victims, each tied to the configuration entry index read from the core's Ready, recording the full durable and in-memory facts; victims restart isolated (the harness throws on any delivery, tested), expected state computed by replaying the durable record through a scratch core; local restore correctness separate from eventual convergence. Distinctness reported both ways: 9 of 9 by host state, 6 of 9 by durable state, the one colliding class (persisted-not-committed, committed-not-applied, conf-applied-not-recorded, joint-entered) declared intentionally indistinguishable with raft-rs citations (commit index volatile, un-persisted apply not durable) and shown to restore identically in both roles. No message is emitted under a new configuration between its in-memory apply and the crash. Lost proposal constructed: leader outbound withheld, no survivor holds the entry, the change never takes effect, the old leader restores with pendingConfIndex 0, a follow-on change commits. Nine persistence-order host mutants killed (3 refused by raft-rs assertions, 2 fail restart equivalence, 4 recorded unsafe). Host contract derived from raft-rs source with file:line per step, split into raftRsGuarantees and hostMustGuarantee, the adapter's write log asserted against it. Contract census in the owner's four categories: MUST SERVE 7, MEMBERSHIP-LOCAL DELETE CANDIDATE 4, DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATION 40, PRODUCTION GAP 12; the forecast counts only the second. Multi-Raft figures labelled preliminary. Two pinned clean builds differ by 177 bytes in the import table only; artifact integrity passes separately. Verdicts derived: consensus core viable, WASM boundary viable, migration undetermined-needs-integration-stage with part A excluded from its inputs. Probe metric 0; the lead recomputed the distinctness figures and the lost-proposal record from the artifact. No production file, dependency version or the owner's raft-logic repository touched; generated-glue exclusions added through the checkers' existing ignore lists, no baseline raised.

round 1 REJECT at staged tree 2346faa5a3c7 (subject byte-identical afterwards; all mutation in copies; crate not rebuilt). The verifier judges the raft-rs CORE good and the EVALUATION not yet sound: 6 blocking defects, all harness or evaluation-claim defects, none a raft-rs defect; several real findings about the WASM boundary. B1 (evaluation-claim + harness; a hosting-model obligation): the honest host loop applies committed entries and writes a durable applied index BEFORE persisting that Ready's HardState; every matrix row has the conf entry alone in its batch so the matrix never sees the consequence; with one normal entry before the conf change, a follower stopped at committed-not-applied or conf-state-recorded-not-advanced leaves durable applied 2, commit 1, last 3 and restart panics 'raft_log.rs:314 applied(2) is out of range [prev_applied(0), min(committed(1), persisted(3))]'. raft-rs documents this by name (src/lib.rs:304-310, read by the lead: persist the commit index with or before applying entries). The artifact instead declared the lagging durable commit isAGap false and rested the intentionally-indistinguishable exemption on the same reasoning - an error the LEAD prompted and accepted. With HardState persisted before apply, committed-not-applied becomes a distinct durable state and the isolated restart re-applies the conf entry from its own log; in the submitted artifact recoveredFromOwnLogAlone is false in all 18 rows, so reconstruction from the peer's own durable log was never exercised. B2: ConfState and applied index are not written atomically; at conf-state-recorded-not-advanced, joint-committed and joint-left the durable ConfState is new with applied below the conf index - the state the harness's own mutant classifier calls unsafe - and after reconnection the core refuses re-application ('config is already joint', 'can't leave a non-joint config'), which the harness catches and swallows and the record does not surface. B3: localRestoreCorrectness is circular - entitledConfState is the same create_node on the same record; corrupting the durable record (added voter, dropped voter) is red locally in only 8 of 18 rows, learner-into-voter is silently accepted on joint-entered, applied-behind silently accepted in 16 of 18, HardState term/vote dropped silently accepted in all 18, and persisting commit but never term or vote leaves all core tests green - the evaluation cannot see in its own adapter the defect part A charges liferaft with. B4: boundaries assert no distinguishing facts, only that signatures differ; shifting each trigger one Ready, 4 of 36 stay green (joint-entered +1 and joint-left -1 in both roles - the latter passes having crashed before the leave entry existed). B5: not deterministic - the sealed lost-proposal receipt fails about 3 in 40 runs (both survivors campaign in lockstep because tick(30) delivers nothing between ticks; raft-rs's election RNG cannot be seeded through the binding) and regeneration changes newLeaderAfterCrash in 6 rows. B6: the derivation receipt checks shape - every verdict input set false with value viable stays green, no receipt regenerates the artifact, the markdown is not compared to the json; and the core-read receipt is bypassable four ways (literal through a const, deepStrictEqual, length or join, a declared after object). Attacks that held: boundaries are tied to the conf entry under mixed batches; none of the nine host mutants passes silently; citations are genuine; no JS decides quorum, commit or leadership; ids cross exactly as strings up to 2^64-1; part A drives real production owners and no term or vote writer exists in src; census mechanical and the forecast counts only the four membership-local names; constraints clean; performance figures reproduced. Findings about the WASM boundary: a raft-rs fatal inside with_node leaves the handle table borrowed so every later call on ANY handle traps - one group's fatal kills all groups in the one-runtime shape; corrupt base64 conf-entry data decodes through unwrap_or_default into an empty change list, which is a leave-joint request; pendingConfIndex crosses as a JS number and does not clear after apply; elections cannot be seeded. Core behaviours a host must know: the core does not check id reuse (identity is wholly a host obligation); propose returning ok means nothing; a proposal whose leader died before persisting can still commit if one follower held it; promotion is not gated on catch-up; the forced-leader change call has no raft-rs equivalent. Isolation window is never challenged (no traffic exists in it). The markdown omits the preliminary Multi-Raft statement, the narrowed re-application statement and any sequential-against-joint section, and says nine distinct host states without the 6 of 9 durable figure. The verifier's own judgment of the three verdicts: consensus core viable; WASM RawNode boundary viable only with named gaps; migration undetermined, no decisive incompatibility found.

Corrective attempt answering verification round 1, by two Opus implementers in sequence (the first exhausted its context; written handover). B1: host order corrected to persist entries and HardState including the commit index BEFORE applying committed entries (raft-rs src/lib.rs:304-310; raft-rs's numbered steps and its example agree with each other and the safety note inside step 3 overrides both - the lead's earlier isAGap false is withdrawn); the old order kept as a mutant that panics raft_log.rs:314; every boundary driven with mixed batches and alone, both victim roles; where the entry is durably committed and not durably applied the isolated restart re-applies it from its own log. B2: ConfState and applied index one atomic durable write; apply_conf_change refusals recorded for the whole run and failing the scenario; the two swallowed round-1 refusals shown absent with a reachability control. B3: 9 durable-record corruptions across the whole boundary matrix, 216 rows, none caught by convergence; oracles named, two independent of create_node and replay (pre-crash core term and vote; survivors' cores); vote-dropped and term-zero caught at every boundary; ConfState rewrites and applied-behind recorded as undetectable from durable state alone at named rows with the host obligation of integrity protection - nothing faked. B4: each boundary asserts its own defining facts relative to the configuration entry, 45 of 45; 42 of 42 one-Ready trigger shifts red; four boundaries added (leave entry durable not applied; lightReady-phase apply; retained follower while joint; auto-leave self-appended before any tick, where the entry is durable on the leader, has_ready false on every peer, and three leader ticks surface it). B5: only the leader ticks and every election is a forced campaign in fixed order; 12 scenarios times 200 runs byte-identical. B6: the derivation receipt rebuilds the artifact and compares it with 13 named measurement keys redacted and type-checked, renders and compares the markdown; verdicts come from a pure function falsified per input; membership values carry a module-private brand from core reads, core returns, the durable record, the requested change or set operations over those, 4,856 fields audited before serialization, and a static census forbids a membership value in any raw assertion - the four bypasses refused; isolation window with real traffic and per-victim counters, delivered 0 in all 45 rows; live hostile per-peer caches and poisoned globals leave ConfState unchanged; static import census. Two harness defects found by the repair itself: the host-mutant classifier was vacuous (entitled voters always empty) - fixed, outcomes now differentiated (4 refused, 2 restart-equivalence-failed, 5 unsafe-recorded); and a raft-rs behaviour - campaigning a peer its own configuration no longer holds panics at raft.rs:1225 - recorded as a named gap. Binding: panic poisoning fixed in the fork with a full bystander scenario, rebuild of the dead group in the same runtime and a leak bound; corrupt conf data now errors; pendingConfIndex a string, the in-progress signal is pendingConfIndex greater than applied. Verdicts derived: consensus core viable; WASM boundary viable-with-named-gaps (open: election RNG unseedable, unstable log not observable through the binding); migration undetermined-needs-integration-stage. The lead re-ran the suite (11 files, 26 assertions green) and read verdicts, mutant outcomes, corruption and trigger-shift records from the artifact. npm test over the whole corpus not yet run. No production file, dependency version or the owner's raft-logic repository touched.

round 2 REJECT at staged tree e348fa2da176 (subject byte-identical afterwards). The verifier's own measurements find the consensus core viable and the WASM RawNode boundary viable with named gaps, migration undetermined, no decisive incompatibility. 4 blocking defects remain: three are the SAME CLASS as round 1 (evaluation receipts that pass while checking shape), narrower and each fixable in tens of lines; the fourth is a new overclaim. CLOSED from round 1: B1 host order (entries and HardState before apply in both the Ready and LightReady phases; 252 of 252 restarts across batches, change styles, roles and shapes the verifier chose, 0 refusals, re-apply from the peer's own log exactly where durable commit reaches the entry and durable applied does not); B2 for the honest loop (0 apply refusals); B4 (180 trigger shifts, 0 green; defining facts are real assertions); B5 (40 of 40 runs, 5 artifact builds differ only in declared measurement keys); B6 derivation (every falsification red); isolation (five leak variants red, per-victim counters real); the surviving exemption legitimate in 42 combinations; 9 citations genuine; constraints clean; wasm digest matches and the artifact contains the fork's strings and exports. BLOCKING 1 (B3, same class): the restore receipt's ConfState oracle is still restored == entitledByDurableState, both through the same create_node; the corruption table's independent oracles are not applied by the restore receipt. Patched into the real receipt path, add-voter and drop-voter are caught locally in 4 of 24 rows and only by convergence in 20 - the artifact claims 18 of 24 locally and the attempt note said none by convergence; a simulated binding bug dropping the learners set on every create_node leaves all 7 restart tests green; an env-var 'service-row cache' injecting a learner into every restored ConfState leaves all 15 core tests green - the owner's 'no service-row cache may repair it' attack succeeds. The rows recorded as undetectable are detectable by the pre-crash core read already recorded, which was not wired. BLOCKING 2 (B6, same class): branded membership arrays are not frozen (empty and refill keeps the brand); changedNodeIds over an invented change mints a branded declared literal because a requested change is never checked against what was proposed to the core; laundering a declared set that way leaves the three-voter receipt and the core-read receipt green after regeneration; the static census misses an aliased assert, a destructure, JSON.stringify, if/throw, indexed loops and computed keys. BLOCKING 3 (same class, and the defect the repair said it fixed): the host-mutant classifier cannot fail - durableIsNew compares a value with itself and is OR-ed with true at core-scenarios.js:2808-2811, so the honest loop and an inert mutant also score unsafe-recorded at one stop; there is no honest control; mutantsKilled cannot be false. The conclusion itself holds - ignoring that stop all 11 mutants are caught at the other two. BLOCKING 4 (new, evaluation-claim + a finding about the binding and hosting model): panic isolation is overclaimed. with_node does fix the RefCell poisoning, but after exactly 304 fatals (deterministic) EVERY call on EVERY group in the runtime traps 'memory access out of bounds' - inferred cause a leaked shared shadow stack per abort, about 3.4 KiB each; the artifact's bound rests on 20 fatals under a redacted key and says blast radius is exactly the group, found-and-fixed, one-runtime STANDS. Correct statement: stands with re-instantiation of the module as the recovery path; fatals are a finite per-instance budget and are REMOTELY triggerable through step - a heartbeat with commit beyond last index from a leader, a non-leader, an unknown peer at a higher term or with to != self; MsgReadIndex with empty entries to a leader; a non-contiguous append; an AppendResponse beyond the leader's last index - so a Multi-Raft host must validate group, recipient and sender before step. Other findings: the removed-peer panic at raft.rs:1225 is reachable only by a host campaign, not by ticks, and its mechanism is mis-stated in the artifact (the real voters vote for the removed peer, the leader is deposed, then the removed peer panics on the winning response); a host campaign on a LEARNER makes it leader; voters grant votes to a non-member, and a ticked removed peer that has not learned of its removal disrupts the group (reached term 28, deposed the leader) - pre_vote and check_quorum are neither configured nor mentioned; re-applying a joint enter or leave is refused, not idempotent, and the applied-behind obligation text says otherwise; a Ready carrying a snapshot leaves durable applied at 0 and the binding exports no snapshot or compaction primitive while fullRawNodeLifecycleExposed is claimed true; raft.rs:962 carries a TODO that auto-leave may never happen if the leader steps down before enter-joint is applied; stepRejections is collected and read by nothing and swallowed a core fatal in one attack; the four-category census is not rendered in the markdown and the forced-leader change sits under DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATION; one document sentence contradicts the artifact's own notCaughtAt table. Non-blocking: redacted cost keys feed no verdict input; victimStillAddressedBySurvivors ignores votersOutgoing; the stale-caches scenario contains no restart and no configuration change; a stale header comment.

Owner decision 2026-09-21 (third addendum to the epic's owner-decision-raft-backend-evaluation record): one FINAL bounded repair round is approved; there is no fourth. The architectural decision no longer depends on this quest - two independent verifiers measured the core viable, the WASM boundary viable with named gaps, migration undetermined with no decisive incompatibility - so the round exists only to make the artifact and receipts certifiable. Fix list frozen to four: an independent restore oracle (pre-crash core state; the cache-derived-learner injection must fail locally); membership provenance tied to the actual core returns and the actual proposed configuration changes instead of a brand; a host-mutant classifier with an honest control that can fail; the panic-isolation and hosting claims withdrawn and replaced by measured runtime re-instantiation and restore at 100 and 1,000 groups plus envelope-only ingress validation before step. The artifact records the backend obligations prominently. Verdict ceilings: core at most viable, WASM boundary at most viable-with-named-gaps, migration exactly undetermined-needs-integration-stage. Stop condition: a rejection on one of the same four defects ends the quest uncertified; an ordinary wording defect is recorded and the evidence packaged; a new substantive incompatibility goes straight back to the owner. No backend integration, no new scenarios beyond the four defects, no fork redesign, no membership-model-reduction work. On approval the evaluation lands locally and the quest raft-rs-experimental-partition-backend is created.

FINAL corrective attempt (owner-approved last round) answering verification round 2, by the second Opus implementer; for each defect the negative control was written first, observed failing against the round-2 code, then the fix, then observed passing. 1 Restore oracle: restore-oracle.js never calls create_node; it compares the FULL ConfState, term, vote and the commit/applied relation against the survivors' core reads where the entry is re-applied from the peer's own log and against the durable ConfState and the victim's own pre-crash core read where nothing is re-applied. Faults injected between crash and restart of real matrix rows: a service-row cache injecting a learner went from missed 24 to caught 24; a binding bug dropping the learners set from missed 7 to caught 7 (17 inert); a truncated outgoing set from missed 3 to caught 3 (21 inert). Ten corruptions through the receipt's own check, 240 rows, no convergence: add and drop voter 24 of 24 (round 2 measured 4 of 24), vote-dropped and term-zero 24 of 24 by the pre-crash core read, applied-ahead and commit-rewound refused by the core, applied-behind 5 of 13 with the 8 misses explained as rows where the restored configuration is still correct; the obligation text now says re-applying a joint enter or leave is refused. 2 Provenance: a ledger records every core read and every proposal when it happens; evidence objects carry a closed-enum sourceKind, operation id, peer, field and a frozen value; changedNodeIds throws unless the ledger saw that exact change proposed; the audit re-checks every evidence object against the ledger; six launderings went from 5 accepted to 6 refused; owner attack 11 fails the audit and the artifact cannot be built from it; 3,259 fields audited, 2 proposals cited and both proposed; test files import no evidence-minting accessor; six syntactic comparison shapes are recorded as known and acceptable because each compares a real core read with a literal. 3 Classifier: the unconditional acceptance removed and the baseline taken from the victim's core before the change; the honest host and an inert switch classify safe at all three stops; all eleven mutants caught and differentiated per stop; mutantsKilled requires both halves. 4 Hosting: the claims 'blast radius is exactly the group', 'found-and-fixed' for the fatal hazard and 'one runtime STANDS' unqualified are withdrawn by name; the fatal budget measured at 303 in the recorded run (299 and 304 in others) before every group traps 'memory access out of bounds'; recovery by a fresh module instance restores 99 of 100 groups in 1.2 ms and 999 of 1000 in 7.9 ms with the one damaged group reported and not retried, labelled preliminary; the owner's hosting sentence recorded verbatim; an envelope-only ingress validator refuses 6 of 9 hostile shapes with zero refusals on honest traffic, and MsgReadIndex with empty entries to a leader still reaches a fatal - recorded as named residue. Artifact: the eight backend-obligation sections and the four-category census rendered; the raft.rs:1225 mechanism corrected and the campaigned-learner-becomes-leader finding added; pre_vote and check_quorum stated as not evaluated here; fullRawNodeLifecycleExposed renamed readyLifecycleExposed with snapshot and compaction a named gap; forced-leader change moved to PRODUCTION GAP; stepRejections read by a census that fails on a swallowed core fatal; cost figures stated to feed no verdict input. Verdict ceilings enforced in the derivation function and its test. Verdicts: consensus core viable; WASM boundary viable-with-named-gaps carrying the five required gaps; migration undetermined-needs-integration-stage. The fork was not rebuilt. The lead re-ran the suite (11 files, 31 assertions), confirmed the unconditional acceptance survives only in a comment and that the withdrawn phrases appear only as the withdrawal and as the status of the two genuinely fixed binding bugs. npm test over the whole corpus not yet run.

round 3 (final) REJECT at staged tree 1e7a3e2d72d2 (subject byte-identical afterwards; the verifier ran out of budget only after delivering its report in full). Two of the same four defects remain, so the owner's stopping condition is met. No new substantive incompatibility was found in raft-rs, WASM hosting, persistent-state recovery, configuration membership or Multi-Raft viability; the verifier's own verdicts are core viable, WASM boundary viable-with-named-gaps, migration undetermined - the rejection is of the receipts and the artifact, not of raft-rs. CLOSED: item 1, the restore oracle is genuinely independent of create_node, picks its oracle by the durable commit/applied relation rather than by boundary name (12 of 45 rows take the survivors branch, 33 the durable-plus-pre-crash branch), and the round-2 create_node patch re-applied verbatim turns the nine-boundary receipt red on every variant, locally, 0 convergence-only and 0 green across all 45 specs; a module-level hook on the glue and a universal conf_state lie are also caught; the fault seam cannot supply an expectation and is asserted disarmed. Item 3, the classifier can fail: the honest host and an inert switch classify safe at all three stops, all eleven mutants are caught with findings true for the stop where they fire, each mutation neutered in a copy becomes passed-silently and the sealed receipt goes red, and mutantsKilled requires both halves. Re-confirmed: host order in both phases, atomic ConfState and applied, 42 of 42 trigger shifts, determinism over 20 runs and 3 artifact builds, the isolation leak, part A on real production owners and excluded from the migration verdict, the verdict ceilings and every falsification, the constraints and the wasm digest, and that the markdown is the rendering of the committed json. BLOCKING 1 (same defect, provenance): trusted membership evidence can still be forged three ways - the durable-record source kind is never checked by ledgerViolation, and durableSnapshotOf returns a branded, unfrozen ConfState whose voters can be rewritten and then minted through membershipArray; the proposal ledger is process-global, keyed by canonical content, recorded before the core call and never value-compared, so a literal change proposed on a throwaway cluster mints branded evidence elsewhere; and witness.tag brands a literal as a core read with no operation id, which the assert helpers accept. Owner attack 11 succeeds through the first two doors: the three-voter scenario's core read replaced by a declared FALSE set of 7,8,9 leaves 30 of 31 tests green after regeneration, with the artifact recording those voters on peers 1, 2 and 3, and the only trace a count nothing bounds. The six syntactic comparison shapes are judged non-blocking in themselves but do leave test files able to reach raw membership.
